The constructs `(([a-zA-Z0-9\-])+\.)+` and the redundant `(...)+` wrapping of `([a-zA-Z0-9]{2,4})+` allow **catastrophic backtracking**. A crafted input such as a long string of alphanumerics with no final match (e.g. `"a@" + "a".repeat(50000) + "!"`) causes exponential evaluation time, letting a remote attacker hang the Node.js event loop with a single request (CVSS 7.5, availability impact).

## Fix

Replace the regex with an equivalent, backtracking-safe pattern that has no nested/overlapping quantifiers, so matching runs in linear time while still validating the same class of addresses (local part, domain labels, 2–4 character TLD).

The root cause of CVE-2024-29409 is that `FileTypeValidator` in `@nestjs/common` validates uploaded files solely by checking `file.mimetype`, which is populated by Multer directly from the client-supplied `Content-Type` header.
